title: Courthouse Picketing (Pen. Code, § 169)

source.release: 2026 Criminal Jury Instructions (as adopted by the Judicial Council, February 2026)

body: The defendant is charged [in Count ______] with (picketing/[or] parading) near a courthouse [in violation of Penal Code section 169].
To prove that the defendant is guilty of this crime, the People must prove that:
1. The defendant (picketed/[or] paraded) in or near a state court building;

2. When the defendant acted, (he/she) did so with the intent (to interfere with, obstruct, or impede the administration of justice/[or] to influence (a/an) (judge[,]/[or] juror[,]/[or] witness[,]/[or] officer of the court) in the discharge of his or her duty).

bench_notes.text: The court has a sua sponte duty to give this instruction defining the elements of the crime.

authority.text: • Similar Statute Constitutional. *Cox v. Louisiana* (1964) 379 U.S. 559, 564 [85 S.Ct. 476, 13 L.Ed.2d 487] [upholding Louisiana statute nearly identical to Pen. Code, § 169].
